title: Personal runtime grok notes
content:
Purpose
Quick brain-dump for a tiny client-side/runtime sketch I keep thinking about: a lightweight personal runtime that helps on-device or client-proxied inference with adaptive priming, budget-aware warmups, and short-lived persona overlays. This is a personal scratchpad rather than an official spec; capture ideas, API shape sketches, config examples, and open questions.

Goals / constraints
- Extremely small surface that app teams can drop into an edge process or local proxy.
- Minimal round-trips: prefer client-only decisions when safe, but allow server-side policy override.
- Cost-sensitivity: warmups, KV caches, and prefill heuristics should be aware of token budgets and latency budgets.
- Privacy: personal overlays should be ephemeral and marked for not-leaking to eval logs; provide strong flags for telemetry.

High-level flow (text diagram)
Client App -> Local Runtime (personal-grok) -> Upstream Proxy / Redwood Ingress
  - local runtime optionally holds small KV cache + persona overlays + priming pipeline
  - runtime decides whether to prefill (warm) based on heuristics and budget
  - if warmup is used, runtime can synthesize a lightweight prefill request with small token window and cached KV prefix

Core components (very rough)
- Prefill Manager: decides when to send warmup prompts, with hysteresis and sampling
- Overlay Store: ephemeral persona/context layers (TTL + staleness score)
- Cost Governor: per-session token budget, soft caps, abort/backoff rules
- Telemetry shaper: masks sensitive fields, flags personal overlays as PII-ish and not to be sent to eval buckets by default

API sketches (HTTP/JSON friendly)
1) Client -> runtime: create session
  POST /v1/personal-sessions
  payload:
    {
      "client_id": "mobile-abc-123",
      "persona_id": "persona:writer-v2",
      "session_ttl_seconds": 3600,
      "budget_tokens": 800,
      "priority_hint": "interactive",
      "privacy_mode": "ephemeral", // ephemeral | persist-local | synced
      "telemetry_opt_out": false
    }
  response:
    {
      "session_id": "psess-xxxxx",
      "warmup_allowed": true,
      "kv_cache_id": "kv-1234"
    }

2) Inference call (high-level)
  POST /v1/personal-sessions/{session_id}/generate
  payload:
    {
      "messages": [ {"role":"user","content":"Write a micro-post about AI ops"} ],
      "max_tokens": 120,
      "temperature": 0.7,
      "use_persona_overlay": true,
      "allow_warmup": "auto" // auto | always | never
    }
  response: streaming token stream or final object. Runtime may inject a short warmup prefix under-the-hood if allowed.

Config sketch: persona overlay format (flat key/value to keep it tiny)
  persona-overlay := list of anchors
  anchor: {
    "anchor_id": "author-tone",
    "type": "system|context|fact",
    "content": "Short single-line guidance",
    "weight": 0.0-1.0,
    "ttl": 600 // seconds
  }
Notes: the overlay system intentionally forbids very large system prompts; ensures size bounds, stores checksums for dedupe, and provides a user-visible expiration.

Priming heuristics (prefill manager)
- Warm if: last inference > 30s AND session budget > 150 tokens AND predicted latency > 150ms
- Sample warmups for interactive surfaces at 20% to avoid cost runaway
- Bias warmup shape: 8-20 tokens, cheap temperature (0.2), short context that stimulates KV cache usage only (not creative text)

Cost governor pseudo-policy
- session_budget = budget_tokens (from create)
- per-call deduction = estimated_response_tokens + warmup_cost
- if session_budget - per_call_deduction < soft_threshold(100): set allow_warmup=false and reduce max_tokens to min(max_tokens, 64)
- if budget exhausted: return polite error + suggested paid-tier link (app may surface)

Telemetry and privacy considerations
- Tag personal overlays with privacy_level=personal; runtime must include explicit consent label before any overlay content is included in telemetry
- Telemetry samples should be client-specified and server-gated: e.g., client telemetry header "telemetry-sample: 0.02" but server may override to 0.0 for privacy-sensitive tenants
- Default: don't include overlay content in traces; only include overlay IDs and hashes. Optionally send overlay text if user opts in and tenant policy allows.

Edge cases and open questions
- How to surface overlay conflicts when both client and server provide persona anchors? Suggest merge precedence: client ephemeral overlays win, but server can mark anchors as "required".
- Should warmups be billable to the hosted API customer or the end user? Need policy. For Dedicated/Private, default to tenant-billed; hosted: tenant unless user pays.
- Offline devices: runtime should be able to run without upstream for trivial prefix rewrites; define a subset of operations that are safe to execute locally (simple template fills, small in-memory model runtime?).

Operational notes / observability hooks
- Expose small debug endpoint: GET /v1/personal-sessions/{id}/state -> returns overlay ids, budget remaining, last_warmup_ts, last_inference_latency_ms
- Instrument events: warmup_sent, warmup_skipped(reason), overlay_expired, budget_limit_hit
- Ensure all debug endpoints respect telemetry_opt_out and do not leak overlay contents unless explicitly allowed

Mini design alternatives considered
A) Heavyweight local runtime with small quantized Llama-like model for offline priming. Pros: full offline experience. Cons: heavy, complex, policy/packaging headaches.
B) Pure orchestration: keep everything server-side but provide client-side heuristics. Pros: simpler to secure. Cons: higher latency and less offline capability.
I favor (B) for MVP and a hybrid for later.

To-dos (short)
- [ ] Quick sketch of overlay schema proto and size/field limits
- [ ] Decide billing policy for warmups and document with billing/growth team
- [ ] Prototype warmup sampling in local dev env, measure cost impact (simulate 10k DAU, 20% warmup sampling)
- [ ] Add unit tests for privacy flags (telemetry opt out)

Random notes / heuristics (brain-dump)
- Make warmups cheap: token-length 8, max temp 0.2, use small context vectors, sampling to reduce deterministic churn
- Always allow clients to pass a short client-side seed hint to make priming deterministic across retries
- Small risk: model stealing signatures in overlay text; prefer checksums instead of raw text in logs

Questions for reviewers
- Would SRE be comfortable with a 20% warmup sampling on interactive endpoints? (Marco: tag you here to sanity-check)
- Is the telemetry tagging strategy compatible with our current ingestion pipeline? (Evan: quick yes/no?)

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating.
